messages:
maria: Anyone else seeing intermittent DNS failures for headless services on edge nodes? Started after last night's GPU drain on node-pool-edge-2. Pods on that pool can't resolve SRV records reliably.
ajay: Yup noticed it too, noticed a spike in 5xx from inference workers that call the router service. svc discovery timing out.
kai: What do logs show from coredns on those nodes? Any upstream NXDOMAIN or SERVFAIL?
maria: coredns logs show lots of "no such host" for cluster.local for headless pods, but only when querying from pods that hit the node-local kube-proxy. HostNetwork pods are fine.
olivia: Could be endpoint slices not being populated to that node. We had a kubelet + kube-proxy restart during the drain, maybe sync didn't finish.
ajay: I grabbed `kubectl get endpointslices -n infra router` and some slices have empty addresses for that AZ. But other zones look normal.
kai: Reproduced locally with `dig +short SRV _router._tcp.router.svc.cluster.local` from a pod on pool-edge-2 -> sometimes returns nothing, sometimes returns records.
maria: Also seeing asymmetric NAT: packets go out via the node egress IP but return path is routed differently, causing kube-proxy hairpin issues sometimes. Suspect iptables conntrack entries are flapping after the GPU drain re-attach.
olivia: Can we check conntrack? `sudo conntrack -L | grep <router-pod-ip>` on one of the edge nodes. I can run if someone gives me a node name.
ajay: Node: node-edge-2a. Running `conntrack -L | wc -l` shows a huge bump right around the drain time.
kai: I saw kube-proxy logs with "skipping stale endpoints" and a bunch of "failed to restore service" messages. Might be endpointSlice controller lag combined with kube-proxy's ipvs sync window.
maria: Quick mitigation idea: enable fallback to service VIPs for that AZ via iptables mode on kube-proxy, or temporarily drain traffic off that pool. But VIP fallback increases latency for chit-chat paths.
olivia: For a short fix, can we scale up a warm GPU pool in another AZ and shift traffic? We have spare capacity in us-west-2a.
ajay: I'll open a canary route to redirect 10% of router traffic to us-west-2a. Deploying patch now. :gear:
kai: For a proper fix we should: 1) reconcile endpointSlice controller health checks, 2) ensure kube-proxy restart order doesn't drop slices, 3) add an egress SNAT sticky routing rule so return path matches.
maria: Agree. Also let's add a healthcheck in the node drain playbook to wait for endpointSlice propagation to all nodes before marking drained. Could avoid this class of race.
sre-bot: Incident created: #INC-2024-342 — edge headless dns intermittent after gpu drain. Severity: medium. Assigned: eng-infra oncall.
olivia: I'll followup with a postmortem draft once we stabilize. For now can everyone keep monitoring `dig SRV` and `kubectl get endpointslices -w` on the affected nodes?
ajay: Monitoring dashboards updated, alerting threshold lowered for unresolved SRV > 5% in last 5m.
kai: Adding a quick script to assert endpointSlices have non-empty addresses across AZs: `for ns in infra; do kubectl get endpointslices -n $ns -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name}:{.endpoints[*].addresses}\n{end}' ; done`
maria: Thanks. If the canary holds we'll failover the remainder and keep a drain fix in the next infra patch. :thumbsup:
